review.rationale: The supplied Gold is a coherent independent planning expectation for the original PRD. REQ-001, AC-001 through AC-003, the repository identity/base commit, and the seven evidence stages agree. The exact four-file writable binding scope covers the runtime implementation, maintained declarations, runtime regressions, and tsd regressions without requiring unnecessary edits. Complete implementation/declaration evidence establishes the shared-engine and shared-options isolation risks; package.json establishes the separate xo, ava, and tsd validation entry points. The disclosed truncation of existing test excerpts does not prevent assessing these planning expectations. TASK-IMPLEMENT and the dependent, independent TASK-VERIFY agree with the specification. Their allowed agents have suitable delivery roles, available slots, and supplied active project-scoped trusted claims for the relevant API, data, state, asynchronous integration, consumer, language, failure-handling, and testing capabilities; the verifier additionally has testing.verification. Pending security.authorization claims are not treated as trusted or needed for this feature. A separate active project reviewer is configured for the high-risk review prerequisite. No material unresolved DEC-001 or hypothetical C input is present in this case, so the empty decision input and ready expectation are consistent. The source fingerprint domains and PRD trim normalization explain the differing source/PRD digests, and the Gold and preview release fingerprints agree across repository, source, team, decisions, prompts, model, sampling, budgets, and metric policy. This assessment relies on the supplied Service-bound provenance, not independent digest recomputation, code execution, or new human attestation. The retained historical operation on the reused project is not treated as a candidate result; no candidate outputs were supplied or used. Approval concerns the Gold expectation only, not task dispatch, execution success, or completion of release preparation.
